title: Grateful Dead Live at Frost Amphitheatre - Stanford University on 1982-10-09
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/88.2k) -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Sony ECM-220T -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Fuji Metal Tape/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: A crystal‑clear audience recording of a 1982 show that dazzles on The Other One, Morning Dew and Eyes of the World, but suffers from uneven playing throughout.
ai_review.review: The tape is praised for its astonishing clarity—often described as sounding like a stereo soundboard—even though it’s an audience source with Phil’s bass and Brent’s keys a bit low in the mix. Musically the night is divisive: some listeners love the fun, tight moments in Throwing Stones, The Other One and Morning Dew, while others criticize sloppy chord changes, weak vocals and a lackluster first set.

ai_rating.rationale: Recording quality is consistently rated excellent; show performance receives mixed feedback, pulling the overall rating to an average‑plus level.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Exceptionally clear tape that many say sounds like a stereo board; minor issues include Phil’s bass and Brent’s keyboards being low in the mix, but overall crystal‑clear sound.

poor_songs: Throwing Stones > Touch of Grey combo
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as flat and plain, while the second set picks up with a few high points (The Other One, Eyes, Morning Dew) despite overall uneven playing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Some reviewers note his guitar tone is clear but his vocals sounded blown, tired and forced; others praise his lead articulations on this tape.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is low in the mix with little punch, making it hard to hear his usual power.
band_member_comments.Bob: Criticized for wrong notes, over‑dramatic singing and sloppy playing, yet also called rhythmically interesting by a different reviewer.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s early‑80s electric piano sounds cheap and sits low in the mix; missing the richer Rhodes/B‑3 tone of earlier years.
